title: 5 Best Option Chain Analysis Tools in India for Nifty and Sensex
summary: Compare five option chain analysis tools for Nifty and Sensex. See which offer live OI, historical quotes and replay, using one real expired Nifty put.
body_markdown:
Where you look up an option depends on the question. If you want the open interest at a Nifty strike today, start with a live option chain. If you want to know what that option traded at yesterday at 11:00 am, open a historical replay.


The best option chain analysis tools in India are NSE, AlgoTest, Sensibull, Opstra and Quantsapp, and each answers a different question. NSE is a useful first stop for official Nifty data.[AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/) gives you free live Sensex and Nifty option chains, and lets you follow a strike through a past session.[Sensibull](https://algotest.in/blog/sensibull-alternatives-india) is useful for comparing open interest across strikes, Opstra for testing a position in five-minute steps, and Quantsapp for studying historical quotes and Greeks.

## Which Option Chain Tool Should You Use?

NSE India


Checking an official Nifty or Bank Nifty figure


Calls and puts by expiry and strike, with volume, open interest (OI) and implied volatility (IV). The historical contract report gives one row per trading day.


The public chain and daily reports are free. Use BSE for the official Sensex chain.


AlgoTest


Live Sensex and Nifty chains, and replaying an expired option


Free live Sensex and Nifty option chains with call and put prices, OI, IV and Greeks across strikes and expiries. For a past session, pick a trading date, expiry, strike and time in the Option Simulator and step forward one minute at a time.


A free account lets you start using the Simulator. The separate Charts tab shows the current date on the free plan, and chart history for earlier dates needs a paid plan. **\[Confirm both access details with the product team.\]**


Sensibull


Comparing OI changes across strikes


Select strikes on the OI, change-in-OI and IV charts to see whether activity was concentrated at one strike or spread across several.


Its free plan includes the basic chain. Its Pro features include live options charts and multi-strike OI analysis.


Opstra by Definedge


Reviewing a position at five-minute intervals


The chain shows IV, OI, volume and Greeks. Its intraday Options Simulator lets you build a position from the chain and follow it in steps of five minutes or more.


Definedge lists the simulator under Opstra Pro. Five-minute steps suit an 11:00 to 11:05 comparison.


Quantsapp


Researching historical bid, ask, IV and Greeks


Its historical Nifty dataset includes the best buy and sell quotes, premium, OI and Greeks by strike, which helps when you need the quotes on either side of the last trade.


The live chain is included in the free tier. Historical backtesting is a separate feature, so check your plan and the history available for your index.


## For a Live Chain, Compare One Row Before Comparing the Whole Screen


Open the[Nifty option chain](https://algotest.in/nifty-option-chain) and the same expiry on NSE. Choose one strike and one side, such as the call, and read the last traded price (LTP), volume and OI across that row.


[Volume](https://algotest.in/blog/how-to-read-volume-in-an-option-chain/) counts contracts traded during the session. OI counts contracts still open. A strike can trade heavily even when its OI barely changes.


If two screens show different numbers, check the quote time first, then the units. NSE displays volume and OI in contracts, while a platform showing the underlying quantity can display a much larger number for the same position.


Also check what each screen means by “[change in OI](https://algotest.in/blog/how-to-read-sensex-oi-data/) ”. A change since the previous close and a change since 10:00 am cover different periods.


For a detailed walkthrough, read[Sensex Option Chain Explained: How to Read, Analyse and Trade Using Live Data](https://algotest.in/blog/how-to-read-and-analyse-sensex-option-chain/)


## Checking a Sensex Strike


Sensex options trade on BSE, so NSE’s chain won’t show them. Open the[live Sensex option chain](https://algotest.in/sensex-option-chain) on AlgoTest and pick the expiry yourself, because a “nearest expiry” shortcut can quietly switch contracts when you move to another trading date.


Then read one row the same way you would for Nifty: LTP, volume and OI for a single strike and side. Sensex contracts have their own expiry day and lot size, so check both before you compare position sizes with a Nifty trade.


> Compare call and put OI, IV and Greeks for every Sensex strike on the[AlgoTest Sensex option chain](https://algotest.in/sensex-option-chain) .


## A Real Nifty Put With Two Different End-of-Day Prices


Take the Nifty 22,600 put expiring 6 June 2024. On 4 June, its daily closing price was ₹878.30, while its last traded price was ₹810.15.


That’s a ₹68.15 difference per unit for the same strike, expiry and trading day. Both figures appear in the historical contract record under different columns, and you can look up the row in NSE’s historical contract-wise price and volume report.


If your question is…


Use this field or view


What closing price did the daily record show?


The Close column: ₹878.30


What was the last trade recorded for the day?


The LTP column: ₹810.15


What was the premium at 11:00 am IST?


The 11:00 intraday snapshot for the 22,600 put. The daily row gives no price for that minute.


What price could a buyer have seen quoted at 11:00?


The best ask at that time, if the historical feed includes quotes. A recorded last trade alone can’t show the available buy price.


## How to Compare the Same Option in Two Replay Tools


In the[AlgoTest Option Simulator](https://algotest.in/feature/simulator?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=seo&utm_campaign=simulator&utm_source=blog&utm_medium=seo&utm_campaign=simulator) , set the trading date to 4 June 2024 and the time to 11:00 am IST. Set the underlying to Nifty, the expiry to 6 June 2024, the strike to 22,600 and the option type to PE (put).


Record the premium and the field label, then enter the same contract and timestamp in a second tool. If it shows a five-minute candle, check whether 11:00 labels the start or the end of that candle before you compare its close with a snapshot.


Advance to 11:05 am with the strike fixed. If a tool automatically follows the at-the-money strike as Nifty moves, it may switch contracts, so keeping 22,600 selected lets you follow the option you started with.


For this exercise,[AlgoTest](https://algotest.in/) lets you step through the minutes in between, while Opstra’s documented five-minute interval fits the two endpoints. If both tools show the same last trade but you want to know what it might have cost to buy the put, use Quantsapp’s historical quotes to check the bid-ask spread.

### FAQs


#### Which free option chain analysis tool should I use for Nifty?


NSE’s public chain is a good starting point for checking a strike’s OI, volume, IV and premium. AlgoTest, Sensibull and Quantsapp also offer a live chain for free. Check historical coverage separately if you need an expired contract at a particular minute.


#### Can I download a historical option chain in Excel?


NSE offers CSV downloads that open in Excel. Its contract-wise report covers one contract over a date range, and its daily F&O bhavcopy contains rows for many contracts on one day.


For the chain at 11:00 am, you need intraday data with timestamps. Check whether the provider offers an export if a spreadsheet is essential.


#### Can I use the NSE option chain for Sensex options?


No. Sensex options trade on BSE, so they don’t appear on NSE’s chain. Use BSE’s equity derivatives chain for the exchange record, or the free[Sensex option chain](https://algotest.in/sensex-option-chain) on AlgoTest to compare call and put OI, IV and Greeks across strikes and expiries.


#### Can I replay an expired Sensex option?


Yes. In the AlgoTest Option Simulator, set the underlying to Sensex, pick the trading date, expiry, strike and time, then step forward minute by minute to see how the premium moved.
